basics.q: What type of blockchain is Retium?
basics.why: Retium describes itself as a multi-dimensional Layer-1 blockchain.

basics.q: What is Retium built around mathematically?
basics.why: Retium uses prime-number mathematics as a foundation of its architecture.

basics.q: What is Retium's network architecture called?
basics.why: Retium calls its multi-directional mesh architecture PrimeMesh.

basics.q: What language was the Retium protocol written from scratch in?
basics.why: Retium states that its Layer-1 implementation was written from scratch in Rust.

basics.q: Is Retium a fork of another blockchain?
basics.why: Retium says its protocol and architecture were built from scratch and are not a fork.

basics.q: Which use case is explicitly listed for Retium?
basics.why: Payments are a listed Retium use case.

basics.q: Which entertainment use case is listed?
basics.why: Gaming is a listed use case.
The use-cases page highlights weight-1 transactions for micropayments.

basics.q: What can be recorded as lightweight social transactions?
basics.why: Retium lists tips, follows, reactions, badges, and subscriptions as social use cases.

basics.q: What kind of machine activity is mentioned for IoT?
basics.why: Retium lists autonomous machine-to-machine payments for smart devices.

basics.q: Which marketplace feature can RCP-1 support?
basics.why: Commerce and marketplace workflows can include escrow and royalties.

basics.q: What is the Retium Foundation focused on supporting?
basics.why: The Foundation supports development, governance, infrastructure, and long-term stewardship of the protocol.

basics.q: Is the Retium Foundation the same entity as Retium AU?
basics.why: The Foundation page explicitly says it is separate from Retium AU.

basics.q: Does RTM confer ownership rights in the Foundation?
basics.why: The Foundation disclaimer says RTM does not confer ownership rights.

basics.q: What should support long-term protocol growth according to the Foundation model?
basics.why: The Foundation emphasizes real network activity supporting real network growth.

mesh.q: How do most traditional blockchains arrange blocks?
mesh.why: Retium contrasts its mesh with the traditional one-block-at-a-time linear model.

mesh.q: Can Retium process multiple blocks at the same time?
mesh.why: PrimeMesh allows multiple valid blocks to process transactions simultaneously.

mesh.q: What determines where blocks exist in Retium?
mesh.why: Prime-number mathematics determines valid block positions.

mesh.q: What is every Retium block ID derived from?
mesh.why: Every block ID is derived from prime factorization and mathematical composition.

mesh.q: What does each tick introduce into PrimeMesh?
mesh.why: Each tick introduces a new prime number.

mesh.q: How are Retium blocks linked in the mesh?
mesh.why: Blocks connect through shared prime factors.

mesh.q: Is Retium's mesh structure deterministic?
mesh.why: The mesh structure follows deterministic mathematical rules.

mesh.q: Does Retium rely on randomness to determine valid block structure?
mesh.why: Retium says there is no randomness, lottery, or luck in its block structure.

mesh.q: Can two nodes verify the expected mesh structure independently?
mesh.why: Anyone running the same calculations can independently verify which blocks should exist.

mesh.q: What helps Retium scale as usage grows?
mesh.why: Retium processes multiple blocks in parallel instead of one block at a time.

mesh.q: What happens to the mesh as new primes are introduced?
mesh.why: New primes generate new valid block IDs and expand the mesh.

mesh.q: What is Retium designed to avoid as a core bottleneck?
mesh.why: Retium replaces the linear one-block-at-a-time model with a multi-directional mesh.

mesh.q: What is a block's position based on?
mesh.why: A block's position and relationships are calculated from prime-number logic.

mesh.q: What does Retium call its approach to block geometry?
mesh.why: Block positions are defined through mathematical prime-factor relationships.

mesh.q: What does 'Direct Routing' mean in Retium?
mesh.why: Retium routes transactions directly to open blocks.

mesh.q: Does Retium use a traditional mempool?
mesh.why: Transactions are routed directly into open blocks rather than waiting in a mempool.

mesh.q: What transaction ordering principle does Retium describe?
mesh.why: The site describes transaction handling as first-come, first-served by design.

mesh.q: What is one core goal of Retium's original architecture?
mesh.why: Retium's architecture is designed to address blockchain scalability from the ground up.

mesh.q: What consensus model does Retium use?
mesh.why: Retium introduces Proof of Math (PoM).

mesh.q: What does PoM stand for?
mesh.why: PoM is Retium's abbreviation for Proof of Math.

mesh.q: In Proof of Math, what determines which blocks can exist?
mesh.why: Retium says mathematics determines which blocks can exist.

mesh.q: In Proof of Work, block structure is associated with what?
mesh.why: Retium contrasts PoW with PoM by describing PoW as energy-driven.

mesh.q: In Proof of Stake, block structure is influenced by what?
mesh.why: Retium contrasts PoS with PoM by describing PoS as influenced by stake ownership.

mesh.q: Do Retium validators choose the mathematical block structure?
mesh.why: Validators execute what the deterministic math dictates.

mesh.q: Does Proof of Math use a mining race?
mesh.why: Retium states there is no mining race.

mesh.q: Does Proof of Math use leader election for block structure?
mesh.why: Retium states there is no leader election in its PoM block structure.

mesh.q: Does Retium use a longest-chain rule?
mesh.why: Retium does not use a longest-chain rule.

mesh.q: How does Retium describe its finality model?
mesh.why: Retium contrasts its deterministic finality with probabilistic models.

mesh.q: What makes competing block positions invalid in Retium?
mesh.why: Each valid block position is uniquely constrained by prime-number relationships.

mesh.q: How does Retium describe fork risk under Proof of Math?
mesh.why: Retium states forks are mathematically impossible under its block-structure rules.

mesh.q: What do validators do after math determines valid structure?
mesh.why: Validators execute what the deterministic math dictates.

mesh.q: What information about a block is calculated deterministically?
mesh.why: Retium says position, parent links, and relationships are calculated deterministically.

mesh.q: What creates a verifiable network structure in Retium?
mesh.why: Independent nodes can derive the same structure from the same math.

mesh.q: What property replaces probabilistic block selection in Retium?
mesh.why: Retium uses mathematical determinism rather than probabilistic block selection.

mesh.q: What does Retium say is absent from block creation logic?
mesh.why: The architecture page explicitly says there is no randomness, lottery, or luck.

mesh.q: What is the key input to block identity in PrimeMesh?
mesh.why: Block IDs are derived from prime-number factorization.

mesh.q: What can anyone independently calculate in Retium?
mesh.why: Anyone can run the same calculations to verify expected block existence.

mesh.q: What kind of guarantee does Retium emphasize for finality?
mesh.why: Retium presents deterministic finality as mathematical certainty rather than probabilistic guarantees.

mesh.q: Does Retium copy Ethereum's consensus model?
mesh.why: Retium says its architecture and consensus were designed specifically for Retium.

mesh.q: What separates Retium from a conventional single-chain model?
mesh.why: PrimeMesh is multi-directional rather than a single linear chain.

mesh.q: What enables many valid blocks to coexist?
mesh.why: Prime-linking relationships allow multiple valid blocks to exist simultaneously.

mesh.q: What must two honest nodes derive when using the same Retium calculations?
mesh.why: Deterministic calculations should lead nodes to the same valid mesh structure.

mesh.q: Which Retium property is intended to make block structure verifiable?
mesh.why: Determinism makes the expected block structure independently verifiable.

routing.q: Where is a new Retium transaction routed?
routing.why: Transactions are routed directly into open blocks.

routing.q: What component routes transactions to blocks?
routing.why: The Router assigns transactions directly to open blocks.

routing.q: How many blocks are typically open at once?
routing.why: Retium says typically 3 to 20 blocks are open depending on traffic.

routing.q: What adjusts the number of open blocks?
routing.why: RouterHelper dynamically adjusts open-block count.

routing.q: What does Retium use to balance computational load when routing?
routing.why: Transactions are assigned to blocks by weight to balance computational load.

routing.q: Does Retium prioritize transactions through gas bidding?
routing.why: Retium uses weight-based fees and does not use gas auctions.

routing.q: What attack vector is reduced by having no mempool?
routing.why: Retium says no mempool removes mempool-based front-running opportunities.

routing.q: What status does a transaction reach immediately after execution?
routing.why: Transactions reach SoftFinal immediately after execution.

routing.q: Who cross-validates transaction state after SoftFinal?
routing.why: Workers cross-validate the post-execution state.

routing.q: What status follows successful Worker consensus?
routing.why: After Worker consensus, the transaction reaches HardFinal confirmation.

routing.q: When do pending receiver funds become spendable?
routing.why: Once consensus is reached, pending funds become spendable.

routing.q: How does Retium describe a HardFinal transaction?
routing.why: HardFinal is described as permanent and cryptographically irreversible.

routing.q: Is transaction finality separate from block finality?
routing.why: Retium separates transaction confirmation from later block finality.

routing.q: Which role handles block finality after transaction confirmation?
routing.why: Block finality is handled later by Suits.

routing.q: What is one benefit of separating transaction and block finality?
routing.why: Transactions can confirm quickly while the block continues through its lifecycle.

routing.q: What is the block lifecycle sequence shown by Retium?
routing.why: Retium shows blocks moving from Planned to Open to Sealed.

routing.q: What advances only after the current mesh phase is finalized?
routing.why: The network advances to the next tick after the current phase is finalized.

routing.q: What fee model does Retium use?
routing.why: Retium uses a weight-based fee model.

routing.q: What is Retium's transaction weight range?
routing.why: Transactions and contracts use weights from 1 to 5.

routing.q: Does Retium use gas auctions?
routing.why: There are no gas auctions.

routing.q: Does Retium use bidding wars for fees?
routing.why: Retium says there are no bidding wars.

routing.q: What percentage of transaction fees is burned?
routing.why: One percent of fees is burned.

routing.q: What percentage remains after the 1% burn?
routing.why: After the 1% burn, 99% remains for network distribution.

routing.q: What is the USD fee for a weight-1 simple transfer?
routing.why: Tokenomics lists weight-1 simple transfers at one cent.

routing.q: What is the USD fee for weight 2?
routing.why: Tokenomics lists weight 2 at five cents.

routing.q: What is the USD fee for weight 3?
routing.why: Tokenomics lists weight 3 standard contracts at ten cents.

routing.q: What is the USD fee for weight 4?
routing.why: Tokenomics lists weight 4 complex DeFi at twenty-five cents.

routing.q: What priority increase is Level 1?
routing.why: Retium lists optional Level 1 priority credits at +10%.

routing.q: What priority increase is Level 2?
routing.why: Retium lists optional Level 2 priority credits at +20%.

validators.q: How many validator roles does Retium define?
validators.why: Retium defines Keepers, Workers, and Suits.

validators.q: Which role validates individual transactions?
validators.why: Workers validate transactions before they become final or rejected.

validators.q: Which role plans blocks?
validators.why: Keepers plan blocks.

validators.q: Which role stores the full mesh state?
validators.why: Keepers store the full mesh state.

validators.q: Which role manages tick advancement?
validators.why: Keepers manage tick advancement.

validators.q: Which role coordinates block finality?
validators.why: Suits coordinate block finality.

validators.q: Which role verifies deterministic Keeper consensus?
validators.why: Suits verify deterministic Keeper consensus.

validators.q: Which role synchronizes the network on each block verdict?
validators.why: Suits synchronize the network on each block's verdict.

validators.q: Which validator role is the lightest by design?
validators.why: Workers are the lightest validator role.

validators.q: Are Workers designed to be stateless?
validators.why: Workers are described as stateless and holding current vote assignments only.

validators.q: Which role has the heaviest hardware requirements?
validators.why: Keepers hold full mesh state and run on GPU-capable server hardware.

validators.q: What level of hardware does a Suit require?
validators.why: Suits have moderate compute and storage requirements.

validators.q: What devices could Workers potentially run on?
validators.why: Retium says Workers could potentially run on phones, tablets, and laptops.

validators.q: How many Workers are assigned to check a transaction?
validators.why: The Matchmaker assigns five Workers.

validators.q: What is the minimum Worker quorum for transaction-level finality?
validators.why: At least three of the five Workers must approve.

validators.q: What component assigns Workers to transactions?
validators.why: The Matchmaker assigns Workers dynamically.

validators.q: How many Suits are assigned to each sealed block?
validators.why: Five independent Suits are assigned to each sealed block.

validators.q: What do Keepers do after a block is sealed?
validators.why: Keepers independently recompute the same mathematical result from the same inputs.

validators.q: What level of Keeper agreement is required for cryptographic consensus?
validators.why: A majority of Keepers must agree.

validators.q: What does a Suit broadcast after required Keeper consensus?
validators.why: A Suit broadcasts the finality verdict.

validators.q: What happens to a block after the Suit finality verdict?
validators.why: After the finality verdict, the sealed block becomes HardFinal.

validators.q: Are blocks sealed only when they are full?
validators.why: Blocks are sealed on a fixed cycle, not only when full.

validators.q: Why are blocks sealed on a fixed cycle?
validators.why: Fixed-cycle sealing helps keep network rhythm predictable.

validators.q: What token is minted when RTM is staked?
validators.why: Staking RTM mints an equal amount of Pie.

validators.q: At what ratio is Pie minted for staked RTM?
validators.why: Pie is minted 1:1 with staked RTM.

validators.q: What happens to Pie when RTM is unstaked?
validators.why: Corresponding Pie is burned on unstake.

validators.q: What backs each Pie token?
validators.why: Every Pie is backed by exactly one RTM locked in staking.

validators.q: What does Pie represent?
validators.why: Pie represents validator commitment.

validators.q: Does Pie support delegation?
validators.why: The tokenomics page says Pie supports delegation.

wallet.q: What is Retium's native coin?
wallet.why: RTM is the native coin of the Retium network.

wallet.q: What is RTM used to pay?
wallet.why: RTM is used for network transaction fees.

wallet.q: Can RTM be used for smart contract interactions?
wallet.why: RTM is used for smart contract interactions.

wallet.q: Can RTM be used for value transfer?
wallet.why: Value transfer is one of RTM's core uses.

wallet.q: What is RTM's fixed total supply?
wallet.why: Total supply is fixed at 1,000,000,000 RTM.

wallet.q: How many decimal places does RTM use?
wallet.why: Each RTM has 18 decimal places.

wallet.q: What is Retium's inflation rate?
wallet.why: Retium describes permanent 0% inflation.

wallet.q: Can RTM supply be increased after genesis?
wallet.why: The current tokenomics page says there is no minting beyond genesis.

wallet.q: Can an admin key increase RTM supply?
wallet.why: No admin key can increase the fixed RTM supply.

wallet.q: Can a governance vote increase RTM supply?
wallet.why: The tokenomics page says governance cannot increase supply.

wallet.q: How much RTM is allocated to the team?
wallet.why: Retium states there is no team token allocation.

wallet.q: How much RTM is allocated to early investors?
wallet.why: Retium states there is no early-investor token allocation.

wallet.q: How much RTM is allocated to advisers or partners?
wallet.why: Retium states there is no allocation for advisers or partners.

wallet.q: Where does almost the entire RTM supply initially sit?
wallet.why: Almost the entire supply sits in the Safehouse.

wallet.q: What is the Safehouse?
wallet.why: Retium describes the Safehouse as an on-chain reserve.

wallet.q: What is the Safehouse RTM-to-rUSD rate?
wallet.why: The Safehouse exchanges one RTM for one rUSD in both directions.

wallet.q: Does RTM launch through a traditional token sale according to current tokenomics?
wallet.why: The tokenomics page says RTM enters circulation through the Safehouse rather than a token sale.

wallet.q: What is the exception to the supply sitting in Safehouse?
wallet.why: A small locked reserve is used to run founding nodes.

wallet.q: Can the founding-node reserve be sold?
wallet.why: Retium states the founding-node reserve is locked and can never be sold.

wallet.q: Are validator rewards inflation-based?
wallet.why: Retium says there are no inflation-based rewards.

wallet.q: Where does validator income come from?
wallet.why: Current tokenomics says validator income comes from real network fees.

wallet.q: What percentage of all transaction fees does the Treasury receive?
wallet.why: The Treasury receives 5.5% of transaction fees.

wallet.q: What is one purpose of the Treasury?
wallet.why: Treasury funding supports development, security, grants, operations, and long-term programs.

wallet.q: Do Retium testnet coins have monetary value?
wallet.why: The testnet page states test coins carry no value.

wallet.q: Can testnet RTM be moved to mainnet?
wallet.why: Faucet coins cannot be moved to mainnet.

wallet.q: Can testnet balances be wiped between stages?
wallet.why: Retium warns that balances, NFTs, and history may be reset.

wallet.q: What signing feature is listed for the public wallet?
wallet.why: The testnet wallet includes 2FA signing.

wallet.q: What connection feature is listed for the wallet?
wallet.why: The wallet includes dapp connect.

wallet.q: How is a wallet key protected on the web wallet?
wallet.why: The wallet page says the key is encrypted with the user's password.

wallet.q: What can the Retium NFT launchpad do on testnet?
wallet.why: The NFT launchpad supports contract calls, minting, and NFT transfers.

wallet.q: Where do launchpad-minted collections appear in the wallet?
wallet.why: Collections minted on the launchpad appear in the wallet NFT tab.

wallet.q: What format can power Retium NFT contracts?
wallet.why: Game assets and NFTs can be implemented using WASM smart contracts with RCP-1.

security.q: What keeps validator assignments dynamic and unpredictable?
security.why: Matchmaker makes assignments dynamic and unpredictable.

security.q: What helps prevent repeated validator grouping?
security.why: RotationLog prevents repeated grouping.

security.q: What cryptographic signature scheme signs network messages?
security.why: Retium states all network messages are signed with Ed25519.

security.q: What checks validator software integrity?
security.why: Binary attestation is used to ensure software integrity.

security.q: What mechanism penalizes false votes and malicious behavior?
security.why: Slashing penalizes false votes, malicious behavior, and protocol violations.

security.q: What does each validator node verify at startup?
security.why: Each node verifies its own binary signature at startup.

security.q: What key is embedded for startup binary verification?
security.why: Validator nodes use an embedded Ed25519 public key to verify the node binary signature.

security.q: What contract execution format does Retium use?
security.why: Retium uses WebAssembly as its contract execution format.

security.q: Which language is recommended for Retium contracts?
security.why: Rust is recommended due to its toolchain and safety guarantees.

security.q: Can languages other than Rust be used if they compile to WASM?
security.why: Retium is language-agnostic at runtime because contracts compile to WASM.

security.q: Which of these is listed as a possible Retium contract language?
security.why: The developer page lists C++ among languages that can compile to WASM.

security.q: Which Go variant is mentioned for WASM contracts?
security.why: TinyGo is listed as an option for WASM contracts.

security.q: What is Retium's unified contract standard?
security.why: Retium uses RCP-1 as a unified contract model.

security.q: Is RCP-1 just a traditional token standard?
security.why: RCP-1 is described as a contract behavior declaration framework.

security.q: What trait does every Retium contract implement?
security.why: Every contract implements the RetiumContract trait.

security.q: Where is RCP-1 metadata embedded?
security.why: Structured RCP-1 metadata is embedded in the compiled WASM binary.

security.q: What marker identifies embedded RCP-1 metadata?
security.why: RCP_METADATA is the metadata marker used in the binary.

security.q: What can RCP-1 metadata declare?
security.why: RCP-1 metadata includes declared computational weight.

security.q: What is the RCP-1 contract weight range?
security.why: RCP-1 contracts declare a computational weight from 1 to 5.

security.q: What else can RCP-1 metadata include besides weight?
security.why: Metadata includes behavioral traits/capabilities.

security.q: What supports contract upgrade history in RCP-1?
security.why: RCP-1 metadata includes version and evolution chain information.

security.q: Can specific contract fields be locked individually?
security.why: RCP-1 allows specific fields, including logic, to be individually locked.

security.q: What happens once a contract field is locked?
security.why: Locking is irreversible for the locked field.

security.q: What field links a new contract version to the previous one?
security.why: Versioned evolution uses the evolves_from field.

security.q: Is contract state preserved across versions?
security.why: Retium says state is preserved across versions, so no migration is required.

security.q: Where do Retium contracts execute?
security.why: Contracts run in a sandboxed execution environment.

security.q: Can contracts directly access the filesystem?
security.why: Sandboxed contracts cannot access the filesystem directly.

security.q: Can contracts directly access the network?
security.why: Contracts cannot directly access the network.

security.q: Can contracts directly access node internals?
security.why: Contracts interact through controlled host functions instead.

security.q: Which host function reads contract state?
security.why: Retium lists read_state as a controlled host function.

security.q: Which host function writes contract state?
security.why: Retium lists write_state as a controlled host function.

security.q: What execution property should identical inputs and state produce?
security.why: Retium's contract layer is designed for deterministic execution.

security.q: What powers the Retium Virtual Machine?
security.why: The RVM uses the Wasmtime WebAssembly runtime.

security.q: Who develops Wasmtime?
security.why: Wasmtime is a production-grade runtime developed by the Bytecode Alliance.

security.q: What is the fuel limit per contract invocation?
security.why: Each contract invocation has a 100M-instruction fuel limit.

security.q: What happens when contract fuel runs out?
security.why: The runtime traps and the transaction is rolled back when fuel is exhausted.

security.q: What target is used when compiling a Rust contract to WASM?
security.why: Retium's developer workflow compiles Rust to wasm32-unknown-unknown.
